title: What does null instanceof return?
keyPoints: null instanceof AnyType is always false – no NullPointerException
This is defined by the JLS: instanceof on null always returns false
Safe for null checks: if (obj instanceof String s) handles null gracefully
This is why instanceof is preferred over getClass() for type checking in equals()
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level

s1_definition.oneliner: null instanceof AnyType is always false. No exception. This makes instanceof safe as a null-guarded type check.
s1_definition.profdef:
JLS rule:

- `null instanceof X` is always `false` for any type X.
- No NullPointerException is thrown.
- This makes instanceof ideal for safe type checking in equals() implementations.
s1_definition.analogy: Asking "is this empty envelope a passbook?" – the answer is always no, and nobody crashes.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  null instanceof String  → false (always, no exception)
  null instanceof Object  → false (always, no exception)

  Safe in equals(): if (!(o instanceof Account)) return false;
  → null returns false, wrong type returns false, correct type proceeds
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
null instanceof anything is always false with no exception. This makes instanceof the safest way to type-check, especially in equals() implementations.

One sentence to remember: null instanceof is always false, never throws – use it for safe type checking.
